scenario.title: Manual Handling
scenario.summary: Safe lifting and carrying techniques in the warehouse.
scenario.mission: Identify poor manual handling practices. Apply the TILE (Task, Individual, Load, Environment) framework to ensure safe operations.

hazards.title: Incorrect lifting posture
hazards.feedback: Correct. Bending at the waist and twisting is a major cause of back injuries.
hazards.reviewText: Always bend knees and keep back straight.

hazards.title: Obstructed view while carrying
hazards.feedback: Correct. The load is too high, obscuring the worker's vision.
hazards.reviewText: Ensure clear line of sight when carrying loads.

hazards.title: Carrying load away from body
hazards.feedback: Correct. Holding the load away from the body increases strain.
hazards.reviewText: Keep the load close to your center of gravity.

hazards.title: Not using available equipment
hazards.feedback: Correct. The worker is struggling manually when a pallet truck is nearby.
hazards.reviewText: Always use mechanical aids when appropriate.

questions.prompt: What does TILE stand for in manual handling?
questions.explanation: TILE stands for Task, Individual, Load, Environment.

questions.prompt: When lifting a load from the floor, you should...
questions.explanation: Bend your knees and keep your back straight.

options.label: Bend your knees and keep your back straight
Keep legs straight and bend at the waist
Twist your body as you lift

questions.prompt: If a load is too heavy, what is the best immediate action?
questions.explanation: Ask for help or use mechanical lifting aids.

options.label: Use a mechanical aid or ask for assistance

questions.prompt: Where should the heaviest part of a load be positioned when carrying?
questions.explanation: The heaviest side should be closest to your body.

options.label: At the top of the load

questions.prompt: Which environmental factor most affects safe lifting?
questions.explanation: Uneven or slippery floors significantly increase the risk of accidents.
